title: Protocol for data collection on drug use in inpatients
author: Paulo Henrique Santos Andrade
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iqqcdvw
materials: Guidelines Forms 1 and 2 must be used in the first pharmaceutical consultation after hospital admission of the patient: 1. form 1 is aimed at obtaining information on the prior history of ADR of the patient; and 2. form 2 is aimed at obtaining information on the pri or history of use of the drug. Forms 3-6 must be used for the daily recording of information observed in medical prescriptions. 1. form 3 is used to record potential drug interactions; 2. form 4 for registration of off-label drugs prescribed; 3. form 5 for the daily recording of the use of drugs; and 4. form 6 for daily monitoring of prescription errors. Furthermore, form 7 must be used for the registration of abnormal laboratory tests or other suspected adverse events.

steps.title: Collect Patient Demographic and Clinical Data
steps.instruction: Record the patient's basic identification and clinical status upon admission.

substeps.instruction: Document name, weight, gender, age, date of birth, medical chart number, and hospital bed number.
Record date of admission, date of discharge, and if applicable, date of death and whether death was associated with an ADR.
Note the clinical diagnosis.
Identify if the child used industrialized medicine before admission and if they use drugs for continuous use.
Record prior history of ADR for the patient and for first and second-degree family members.

steps.title: Document Prior History of ADR
steps.instruction: Use Form 1 to detail the patient's history of adverse drug reactions.

substeps.instruction: Categorize the occurrence as 'Allergy' or 'Other ADR'.
Record the name of the drug and a brief account of the occurrence.
Indicate if a drug sensitivity test was performed.
Check medical records, prescriptions, and hospital beds for self-reports of ADR.
Verify if the self-reported drug was prescribed and administered to the patient.

steps.title: Perform Medication Reconciliation
steps.instruction: Use Form 2 to reconcile medications used before and after hospital admission.

substeps.instruction: List up to 15 medicines in use before admission, including drug name, dose, route, frequency, and duration of therapy.
Determine if any of these medicines were prescribed after admission.
If prescribed after admission, identify if a medication of the same medicinal class was used and specify the drugs.
Identify and list specific drugs that underwent changes in dose, route, frequency, or duration of therapy.

steps.title: Analyze Potential Drug Interactions
steps.instruction: Use Form 3 to identify and evaluate drug interactions.

substeps.instruction: Identify potential occurrences of drug interactions.
For each interaction, record the gravity, the ADE, and the duration in days.
Calculate the total number of medicinal interactions found.

steps.title: Evaluate Off-Label Drug Use
steps.instruction: Use Form 4 to monitor and report off-label use events.

substeps.instruction: Assess prescriptions as either 'Inadequate prescription' or 'Proper prescription'.
Identify if an off-label use event occurred and provide a detailed report for each instance.

steps.title: Conduct Pharmacotherapeutical Follow-up
steps.instruction: Use Form 5 to track daily drug administration and interactions by month/year.

substeps.instruction: Record the drug, dose, route, and frequency for each day of the month (1-31).
Identify the presence of moderate drug interactions in the prescription.
Identify the presence of serious drug interactions in the prescription.

steps.title: Monitor Prescription Errors
steps.instruction: Use Form 6 to quantify prescription errors daily (1-31) for the month/year.

substeps.instruction: Count drugs missing a dose (not written or uncalculable).
Count drugs missing a route of administration.
Count drugs missing dosage (dose interval).
Count drugs prescribed by trade name.
Count drugs with vague expressions (missing conditions of use, max daily dose, or interruption criteria).
Count drugs with illegible descriptions.
Count injectable drugs prescribed per day.
Count intravenous drugs missing infusion rate or infusion time.
Count drugs (IV, IM, subcutaneous, neuraxial, or nerve plexus) missing diluent type or diluent volume.
Count total prescribed antibiotics and those missing treatment duration.
Calculate the total number of drugs prescribed with errors.

steps.title: Perform Laboratory and Clinical Accompaniment
steps.instruction: Use Form 7 to monitor clinical parameters and toxicity markers.

substeps.instruction: Monitor Hemogram: Hemoglobin (12-17 g/dL), Hematocrit (36-57%), Neutrophils (2000-7700/mm³), Eosinophils (40-660/mm³), Lymphocytes (800-4400/mm³), Monocytes (120-990/mm³), Basophiles (0-200/mm³), and Platelets (150-400.103 K/uL) to detect anemia, myelotoxicity, neutropenia, eosinophilia, lymphocytopenia, monocytopenia, basophilia, or thrombocytopenia.

Monitor Liver Function: AST (10-39 U/L), ALT (10-45 U/L), ALP (0-645 U/L), GGT (5-58 U/L), Direct Bilirubin (0.0-0.4 mg/dL), Indirect Bilirubin (0.0-0.8 mg/dL), Albumin (3.5-5.5 g/dL), and Globulin (3.5-5.5 g/dL) to detect hepatotoxicity.
Monitor Renal Function: Creatinine (0.5-1.2 mg/dL) and Urea (15-45 mg/dL) to detect nephrotoxicity, and Uric acid (1.5-7.0 mg/dL).
Monitor Electrolytes: Sodium (136-145 mmol/L), Potassium (3.5-5.1 mmol/L), Calcium (8.8-11 mg/dl), Magnesium (1.58-2.56 mmol/L), and Chloride (98-110 mmol/L) to detect electrolyte disturbances.
Monitor other markers: LDH (200.0-480.0 U/L) and Lactate (4.5-19.8 mg/dL).

Assess for Pharmacodermia (skin patches, pruritus, hyperemia, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome), Gastrointestinal toxicity (diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, constipation), Neurotoxicity (agitation, seizure, consciousness change, unintentional movement), and Cardiotoxicity (ECG change, tachycardia, hypotension, shock).
